title: Research Q&A
note: 自分の研究について答える。points は答えに入れる要素（どの研究にも当てはまる言い方）。回答例 en / more は架空の研究にもとづく参考で、自分で保存した回答例があればそちらを手本にする。

follow.q: Can you tell me a little more about that?
follow.ja: もう少し詳しく教えてもらえますか。
follow.points: もう一歩具体的な対象や場面を1つ
follow.en: More specifically, we focus on activities at home, such as cooking and sleeping.

follow.q: Can you give me an example?
follow.ja: 例を挙げてもらえますか。
follow.points: 具体例を1つ（誰が・何をすると・どうなる）
follow.en: For example, the system can notice when a person has not moved for a long time.

follow.q: Why are you interested in this topic?
follow.ja: なぜこのテーマに興味があるのですか。
follow.points: 興味を持った理由を1つ（きっかけや役立つ場面）
follow.frame: I am interested in it because ...
follow.en: I am interested in it because it can directly help people in daily life.

cards.q: What is your research about?
cards.ja: あなたの研究は何についてですか。
cards.points: 何を対象に、何を使って研究しているか
cards.en: My research is about recognizing daily activities with wearable sensors.
cards.more: For example, we detect walking and sleeping from a smartwatch. This can help people stay healthy.

cards.q: Can you summarize your research in one sentence?
cards.ja: 研究を1文で要約できますか。
cards.points: 何を提案し、何が良くなるかを1文で
cards.en: In short, we propose a method to reduce the cost of labeling sensor data.
cards.more: The key idea is to use only a small number of labels. It works well on public datasets.

cards.q: What field are you working in?
cards.ja: どの分野で研究していますか。
cards.points: 分野名を1つ（必要なら近い分野も）
cards.frame: I work in the field of ...
cards.en: I work in the field of ubiquitous computing.
cards.more: In particular, I use machine learning to analyze sensor data. I am interested in applications for healthcare.

cards.q: What are you working on now?
cards.ja: 今は何に取り組んでいますか。
cards.points: 今取り組んでいる具体的な作業
cards.frame: Right now, I am working on ...
cards.en: Right now, I am working on improving our model for new users.
cards.more: The current model needs data from each user. I want to remove that step.

cards.q: Who would use your research?
cards.ja: あなたの研究は誰が使うのですか。
cards.points: 使う人（誰が・どんな場面で）
cards.en: It would be useful for older adults who live alone.
cards.more: It can also help their families and caregivers. They can notice problems earlier.

cards.q: What is the key idea of your work?
cards.ja: 研究の中心となるアイデアは何ですか。
cards.points: アイデアの核を1つ（何と何をどうするか）
cards.en: The key idea is to combine data from several cheap sensors.
cards.more: Each sensor is not very accurate. However, together they give reliable results.

cards.q: Can you explain your research to a non-expert?
cards.ja: 専門外の人に研究を説明できますか。
cards.points: 専門用語を使わずに、何ができるようになるか
cards.en: Simply put, we teach computers to understand what people are doing.
cards.more: We use data from a smartwatch. Then the system can give helpful advice.

follow.q: Why has this problem not been solved yet?
follow.ja: なぜまだ解決されていないのですか。
follow.points: まだ解かれていない理由を1つ（何が難しいか）
follow.en: It is difficult because real-world data is noisy and different for each person.

follow.q: How will you know when you have reached your goal?
follow.ja: 目標を達成したと、どう判断しますか。
follow.points: 達成を判断する基準（数値や状態）
follow.en: We will know when the system works well for new users without extra training.

follow.q: Is this a new problem?
follow.ja: これは新しい問題ですか。
follow.points: 新しいかどうか＋なぜ今重要か
follow.en: It is not new, but it has become more important because sensors are now everywhere.

cards.q: What is the main goal of your research?
cards.ja: 研究の主な目的は何ですか。
cards.points: 最終的に達成したいことを1つ
cards.frame: The main goal of my research is to ...
cards.en: The main goal of my research is to detect health problems early.
cards.more: We use data from wearable devices. We want to do this without bothering users.

cards.q: What problem are you trying to solve?
cards.ja: どんな問題を解決しようとしていますか。
cards.points: 今ある問題（何が難しい・何が足りない）
cards.en: The problem is that collecting labeled data takes a lot of time.
cards.more: Because of this, many systems cannot be used in the real world. We want to reduce this cost.

cards.q: Why is this problem important?
cards.ja: なぜこの問題は重要なのですか。
cards.points: 重要な理由（困る人の多さ・影響の大きさなど）
cards.en: This is important because many people have this problem in daily life.
cards.more: Existing solutions are expensive. A simple system could help many more people.

cards.q: What motivated you to start this research?
cards.ja: この研究を始めたきっかけは何ですか。
cards.points: 始めたきっかけ（気づいたこと・経験）
cards.en: I started this research because I noticed that existing systems were difficult to use.
cards.more: Many users stopped using them after a few days. I wanted to understand why.

cards.q: What is your research question?
cards.ja: あなたのリサーチクエスチョンは何ですか。
cards.points: 「〜できるかどうか」の形で問いを1つ
cards.en: My research question is whether we can keep high accuracy with fewer labels.
cards.more: To answer this, we compared several training methods. We tested them on three datasets.

cards.q: What do you want to achieve in the end?
cards.ja: 最終的に何を達成したいですか。
cards.points: 最終的に作りたいもの・実現したい状態
cards.frame: In the end, I want to ...
cards.en: In the end, I want to build a system that anyone can use without experts.
cards.more: It should work at home with cheap devices. That is my long-term goal.

cards.q: Who has this problem?
cards.ja: この問題を抱えているのは誰ですか。
cards.points: 困っている人や場面
cards.en: This is a problem for developers who do not have much data.
cards.more: Large companies can collect a lot of data. Small teams cannot, so they need a different approach.

follow.q: Could you explain that step in more detail?
follow.ja: その部分をもう少し詳しく説明してもらえますか。
follow.points: その部分の中身を1つ具体的に（何を入れて、何をするか）
follow.en: In more detail, the model first splits the data into short windows.

follow.q: How long does it take to run?
follow.ja: 実行にどれくらい時間がかかりますか。
follow.points: かかる時間（何で実行して何秒・何分か）
follow.en: It takes about one second on a normal smartphone.

follow.q: Could a simpler method do the same thing?
follow.ja: もっと単純な手法でも同じことができませんか。
follow.points: 単純な手法との違いを1つ（精度・汎用性など）
follow.frame: A simpler method could work, but ...
follow.en: A simpler method could work, but it would be less accurate for new users.

cards.q: Why did you choose this method?
cards.ja: なぜこの手法を選んだのですか。
cards.points: 選んだ理由を1つ（例：少ないデータでも動く／シンプル／結果を説明しやすい）
cards.en: We chose this method because it works well with limited data.
cards.more: It is also easy to interpret. This is important for our users.

cards.q: How does your method work?
cards.ja: あなたの手法はどのように動きますか。
cards.points: 手順を2〜3段階で（まず… 次に…）
cards.en: First, we collect sensor data. Then, we use a model to classify the activity.
cards.more: Finally, we give feedback to the user. The whole process runs on a smartphone.

cards.q: What is the key component of your system?
cards.ja: システムの鍵となる部分は何ですか。
cards.points: いちばん大事な部品・仕組みを1つ
cards.en: The key component is a small model that adapts to each user.
cards.more: It learns from a few examples. Because of this, the setup is very short.

cards.q: Did you consider other methods?
cards.ja: 他の手法は検討しましたか。
cards.points: 検討した別の手法と、選ばなかった理由
cards.en: Yes, we also considered a larger model, but it needed too much data.
cards.more: It was also too slow for a smartphone. So we chose a simpler one.

cards.q: What tools or devices did you use?
cards.ja: どんな道具や機器を使いましたか。
cards.points: 使った道具・装置と、その用途
cards.en: We used a smartwatch to record the movement data.
cards.more: We also used a smartphone app to collect labels. Both devices are easy to buy.

cards.q: What is the most difficult part of your method?
cards.ja: あなたの手法で一番難しい部分は何ですか。
cards.points: 難しかった点を1つ
cards.en: The most difficult part is dealing with noisy sensor data.
cards.more: The noise is different for each person. We spent a lot of time on this.

cards.q: Is your method easy to implement?
cards.ja: あなたの手法は実装しやすいですか。
cards.points: 実装しやすいか＋理由（使う道具・手間）
cards.en: I think so, because it uses only standard tools.
cards.more: We also plan to release our code. So other researchers can try it easily.

follow.q: Is that enough data?
follow.ja: データはそれで十分ですか。
follow.points: 今の量で言えることと、足りない点
follow.en: It is enough for a first study, but we need more data to generalize.

follow.q: Why did you choose that setting?
follow.ja: なぜその設定を選んだのですか。
follow.points: その設定にした理由（現実に近い・比べやすいなど）
follow.en: We chose it because it is close to how people really use the system.

follow.q: Did you have any trouble during the experiment?
follow.ja: 実験中に何か問題はありましたか。
follow.points: 困ったことを1つ
follow.en: One problem was that some participants forgot to charge the device.

cards.q: How did you collect your data?
cards.ja: データはどうやって集めましたか。
cards.points: 誰（何）から、どれくらいの期間・量を集めたか
cards.en: We collected data from twenty participants for two weeks.
cards.more: They wore a smartwatch in daily life. They also recorded their activities in an app.

cards.q: How did you evaluate your method?
cards.ja: 手法をどのように評価しましたか。
cards.points: 評価に使ったデータや方法
cards.en: We evaluated our method with three public datasets.
cards.more: We compared it with two baseline methods. We mainly used accuracy as the metric.

cards.q: How many participants did you have?
cards.ja: 参加者は何人でしたか。
cards.points: 人数（必要なら条件も）
cards.en: We had twenty participants in our study.
cards.more: Most of them were university students. We want to include older people in the future.

cards.q: What did you compare your method with?
cards.ja: あなたの手法を何と比較しましたか。
cards.points: 比較した手法（ベースライン）
cards.en: We compared our method with two standard methods.
cards.more: They are widely used in this field. We used the same data for all of them.

cards.q: What metric did you use?
cards.ja: どの評価指標を使いましたか。
cards.points: 主な評価指標を1つ
cards.frame: We used ... as the main metric.
cards.en: We used accuracy as the main metric.
cards.more: We also measured the response time. Both are important for real use.

cards.q: How did you get the correct labels?
cards.ja: 正解ラベルはどうやって得ましたか。
cards.points: 正解ラベルをどう付けたか
cards.en: The labels came from the participants themselves.
cards.more: They recorded their activities with an app. We checked some of them with video.

cards.q: Where did you run the experiment?
cards.ja: 実験はどこで行いましたか。
cards.points: 実験した場所・環境
cards.en: We ran the experiment in the participants' homes.
cards.more: A lab is easier to control. However, we wanted to see real behavior.

decks.title: 新規性・先行研究との違い

follow.q: Are there any disadvantages?
follow.ja: 欠点はありますか。
follow.points: 欠点を1つ
follow.en: One disadvantage is that our method takes longer to train.

follow.q: How big is the difference?
follow.ja: その違いはどれくらい大きいですか。
follow.points: 差の大きさ（数値で）
follow.en: The difference is about ten percent in accuracy.

follow.q: Which previous study is the closest to yours?
follow.ja: あなたの研究に最も近い先行研究はどれですか。
follow.points: いちばん近い先行研究と、違う点
follow.en: The closest work is a study that used a similar sensor in a lab.

cards.q: What is the main difference from previous work?
cards.ja: 先行研究との主な違いは何ですか。
cards.points: 先行研究との違いを1つ
cards.en: The main difference is that our method does not need labels from new users.
cards.more: Previous methods need data from each user. Ours works from the first day.

cards.q: What is new about your research?
cards.ja: あなたの研究の新しい点は何ですか。
cards.points: 新しい点を1つ
cards.en: The new point is that we combine two types of sensors in real time.
cards.more: Earlier work used them separately. By combining them, we get better results.

cards.q: How is your work related to previous studies?
cards.ja: あなたの研究は先行研究とどう関係していますか。
cards.points: 土台にした先行研究の流れ
cards.en: Our work builds on earlier studies on activity recognition.
cards.more: We extend them to a new setting. Specifically, we focus on users at home.

cards.q: What is the advantage of your method?
cards.ja: あなたの手法の利点は何ですか。
cards.points: 主な利点を1つ（安い・速い・正確など）
cards.en: The main advantage is that our method is much cheaper.
cards.more: It needs only one sensor. So it is easier to use in many homes.

cards.q: Why didn't previous methods solve this problem?
cards.ja: なぜ従来の手法はこの問題を解決できなかったのですか。
cards.points: 先行研究が置いていた前提や、足りなかった点
cards.en: Previous methods assume that a lot of labeled data is available.
cards.more: In the real world, this is often not true. So they do not work well there.

cards.q: What is your main contribution?
cards.ja: あなたの主な貢献は何ですか。
cards.points: 主な貢献を1つ（手法・データ・知見など）
cards.en: Our main contribution is a new method for learning from few labels.
cards.more: We also provide a new dataset. We hope other researchers will use it.

cards.q: Has anyone tried a similar approach?
cards.ja: 似たアプローチを試した人はいますか。
cards.points: 似た試みがあるか＋自分との違い
cards.en: As far as I know, similar ideas were tested only in the lab.
cards.more: We are the first to test this in real homes. The results were quite different.

follow.q: Is that difference significant?
follow.ja: その差は有意ですか。
follow.points: 差を確かめた方法（統計的検定など）
follow.en: Yes, we confirmed it with a statistical test.

follow.q: Can you explain that result in more detail?
follow.ja: その結果をもう少し詳しく説明してもらえますか。
follow.points: 結果の具体的な数値や中身
follow.en: Specifically, the accuracy went up from seventy to eighty percent.

follow.q: Were you surprised by the results?
follow.ja: 結果に驚きましたか。
follow.points: 驚いたか＋その理由
follow.en: A little, because we expected a much smaller improvement.

cards.q: What are your main results?
cards.ja: 主な結果は何ですか。
cards.points: 主な結果を1つ（何が何より良かったか）
cards.en: The results show that our method outperforms the baseline.
cards.more: The accuracy improved by about ten percent. The improvement was larger for new users.

cards.q: What is your most important finding?
cards.ja: 最も重要な発見は何ですか。
cards.points: 最も重要な発見を1つ
cards.en: We found that a simple model works well with good features.
cards.more: This was surprising to us. It means that we do not always need a large model.

cards.q: How much did the performance improve?
cards.ja: 性能はどれくらい向上しましたか。
cards.points: 改善の大きさ（何と比べて何％など）
cards.en: It improved by about ten percent compared with the baseline.
cards.more: The errors decreased by half in some cases. However, the improvement depends on the dataset.

cards.q: Did you get any unexpected results?
cards.ja: 予想外の結果はありましたか。
cards.points: 予想外だった結果を1つ
cards.en: One unexpected result was that more data did not always help.
cards.more: After some point, the accuracy stopped increasing. We are still investigating the reason.

cards.q: Do the results support your hypothesis?
cards.ja: 結果は仮説を支持していますか。
cards.points: 仮説を支持するか＋その根拠
cards.en: Yes, the results suggest that our idea is correct.
cards.more: However, the effect was smaller than we expected. So we need more experiments.

cards.q: In which case does your method work best?
cards.ja: あなたの手法はどんな場合に最もうまくいきますか。
cards.points: うまくいく条件
cards.en: It works best when only a few labels are available.
cards.more: With a lot of labels, the difference is small. So it is useful in the early stage.

cards.q: In which case does it fail?
cards.ja: どんな場合に失敗しますか。
cards.points: うまくいかない条件
cards.en: It often fails when two activities are very similar.
cards.more: For example, it confuses sitting and standing. We need more information to separate them.

follow.q: How could you check that?
follow.ja: それはどうやって確かめられますか。
follow.points: 確かめる方法（追加の実験など）
follow.en: We could check it by running the same test with outdoor data.

follow.q: Does that apply to other cases too?
follow.ja: それは他の場合にも当てはまりますか。
follow.points: 他の場合に当てはまるか＋まだ確かめていない点
follow.en: I think it applies to similar tasks, but we have not tested them yet.

follow.q: What is the evidence for that?
follow.ja: その根拠は何ですか。
follow.points: 根拠となるデータや観察
follow.en: The evidence is that the errors appeared only in the new environment.

cards.q: Why do you think your method works well?
cards.ja: なぜあなたの手法はうまくいくと思いますか。
cards.points: うまくいく理由を1つ
cards.frame: I think it works well because ...
cards.en: I think it works well because it uses information from each user.
cards.more: People move in different ways. Our model can learn these differences.

cards.q: What does this result mean?
cards.ja: この結果は何を意味しますか。
cards.points: 結果が意味すること
cards.en: This means that we do not need a lot of labels.
cards.more: So new users can start using the system quickly. This makes it more practical.

cards.q: Why did the accuracy drop in this case?
cards.ja: なぜこの場合は精度が下がったのですか。
cards.points: 考えられる原因を1つ
cards.en: One possible reason is that the test environment was different.
cards.more: The model was trained on indoor data. It had never seen outdoor data.

cards.q: How do you explain this result?
cards.ja: この結果をどう説明しますか。
cards.points: なぜそうなったかの説明
cards.en: I think this is because the two classes are very similar.
cards.more: Even humans find it hard to separate them. More sensors may solve this.

cards.q: What can we learn from your results?
cards.ja: あなたの結果から何が学べますか。
cards.points: 結果から言える示唆
cards.en: Our results suggest that simple feedback is better for users.
cards.more: Too much information made them tired. Designers should keep this in mind.

cards.q: Are you sure about that explanation?
cards.ja: その説明に確信はありますか。
cards.points: 確信の度合い＋根拠
cards.frame: I am not completely sure, but ...
cards.en: I am not completely sure, but our data supports this idea.
cards.more: We need another experiment to confirm it. That is part of our future work.

cards.q: Could there be another explanation?
cards.ja: 別の説明は考えられますか。
cards.points: 別の説明の可能性を1つ
cards.en: Yes, another possibility is that the participants got used to the task.
cards.more: We cannot separate the two effects now. A longer study would help.

follow.q: How serious is that limitation?
follow.ja: その限界はどれくらい深刻ですか。
follow.points: その限界の深刻さ＋理由
follow.en: I think it is not so serious because the main results do not depend on it.

follow.q: How would you solve that?
follow.ja: それをどう解決しますか。
follow.points: 解決方法を1つ
follow.en: One way is to collect data from more people of different ages.

follow.q: Does that affect your main conclusion?
follow.ja: それは主な結論に影響しますか。
follow.points: 結論への影響があるか＋理由
follow.en: I don't think so, because the main trend was the same in every group.

cards.q: What are the limitations of your study?
cards.ja: あなたの研究の限界は何ですか。
cards.points: 限界を1つ（人数・期間・環境など）
cards.en: One limitation is that the number of participants is small.
cards.more: Also, all of them were students. So we cannot generalize the results yet.

cards.q: Does your method work in the real world?
cards.ja: あなたの手法は実世界で動きますか。
cards.points: 実環境で試したか＋まだならその予定
cards.frame: We have not tested it in ... yet.
cards.en: We have not tested it in real homes yet.
cards.more: So far, we have used data from a lab. We plan to run a field study next year.

cards.q: What assumptions did you make?
cards.ja: どんな仮定を置きましたか。
cards.points: 置いている前提を1つ
cards.en: We assume that users wear the device all day.
cards.more: If they take it off, the system cannot work. This is a limitation.

cards.q: Can your results be generalized?
cards.ja: 結果は一般化できますか。
cards.points: どこまで一般化できるか＋確かめていない範囲
cards.frame: I think they can be generalized to ..., but ...
cards.en: I think they can be generalized to similar users, but we need to test other groups.
cards.more: Our participants were young. Older people may behave differently.

cards.q: Does it work for all users?
cards.ja: すべてのユーザーでうまくいきますか。
cards.points: うまくいく人・いかない人を分ける条件
cards.frame: Not for all users. It depends on ...
cards.en: Not for all users. It depends on how they wear the device.
cards.more: It works well on the wrist. In a pocket, the accuracy is lower.

cards.q: What is the weakest point of your research?
cards.ja: あなたの研究の一番の弱点は何ですか。
cards.points: 最も弱い点を1つ
cards.frame: I think the weakest point is ...
cards.en: I think the weakest point is the short evaluation period.
cards.more: We observed users for only two weeks. Long-term effects are still unknown.

cards.q: What about privacy?
cards.ja: プライバシーについてはどうですか。
cards.points: プライバシーを守るための工夫
cards.en: To protect privacy, we process the data on the device.
cards.more: We do not send raw data to a server. Still, this is an important issue.

follow.q: What will be the biggest challenge?
follow.ja: 一番の課題は何になりそうですか。
follow.points: 最大の課題
follow.en: The biggest challenge will be finding enough participants.

follow.q: How long will that take?
follow.ja: それにはどれくらいかかりますか。
follow.points: かかる期間（作業の内訳も）
follow.en: It will take about six months, including the analysis.

follow.q: Why is that the next step?
follow.ja: なぜそれが次のステップなのですか。
follow.points: それが次である理由
follow.frame: It is the next step because ...
follow.en: It is the next step because we need real data before we improve the model.

cards.q: What will you investigate next?
cards.ja: 次は何を調べますか。
cards.points: 次に調べること
cards.en: We plan to investigate the long-term effects of the system.
cards.more: We will run a study for three months. We want to see how the behavior changes.

cards.q: What is your next step?
cards.ja: 次のステップは何ですか。
cards.points: 次のステップ（何をどこで評価・開発するか）
cards.frame: As a next step, we will ...
cards.en: As a next step, we will evaluate the system in real environments.
cards.more: We are preparing a study with thirty homes. It will start next spring.

cards.q: How can your method be applied to other fields?
cards.ja: あなたの手法は他の分野にどう応用できますか。
cards.points: 応用できる分野・場面
cards.frame: This method can be applied to ...
cards.en: This method can be applied to healthcare and sports.
cards.more: Any field with sensor data and few labels can use it. We want to try rehabilitation first.

cards.q: How would you improve your method?
cards.ja: あなたの手法をどう改善しますか。
cards.points: 改善したい点と、その方法
cards.frame: I would like to improve ... by ...
cards.en: I would like to improve the accuracy by adding another sensor.
cards.more: The current system uses only one. Sound data may be helpful.

cards.q: What is your long-term goal?
cards.ja: 長期的な目標は何ですか。
cards.points: 長期的な目標
cards.en: My long-term goal is to build systems that support people in everyday life.
cards.more: They should be simple and cheap. I want many people to use them.

cards.q: If you had more time, what would you do?
cards.ja: もっと時間があれば、何をしますか。
cards.points: 時間があればやりたいこと
cards.frame: If I had more time, I would ...
cards.en: If I had more time, I would collect data from more users.
cards.more: I would also run a longer study. Then the results would be more reliable.

cards.q: What do you want to finish before you graduate?
cards.ja: 卒業までに何を終えたいですか。
cards.points: 修了までに終えたいこと
cards.frame: Before I graduate, I want to ...
cards.en: Before I graduate, I want to finish a field study with real users.
cards.more: I also want to publish the results in a journal. After that, I will write my thesis.

decks.title: Ph.D. Forum でよく聞かれること

follow.q: Sorry, could you explain that more simply?
follow.ja: すみません、もっと簡単に説明してもらえますか。
follow.points: 専門用語を使わずに言い直す
follow.en: In other words, the system learns from a small number of examples.

follow.q: What do you need to finish it?
follow.ja: それを終えるには何が必要ですか。
follow.points: 終えるのに必要なもの（人・時間・データ）
follow.en: To finish it, I need more participants and about six more months.

follow.q: What did you learn from that?
follow.ja: そこから何を学びましたか。
follow.points: 学んだこと
follow.en: I learned that it is important to test early with real users.

cards.q: What stage of your Ph.D. are you in?
cards.ja: 博士課程のどの段階にいますか。
cards.points: 博士課程の何年目か
cards.frame: I am in the ... year of my Ph.D.
cards.en: I am in the second year of my Ph.D.
cards.more: I have finished the first study. Now I am working on the second one.

cards.q: What feedback would you like from us?
cards.ja: 私たちからどんなフィードバックが欲しいですか。
cards.points: 助言がほしい点を1つ
cards.en: I would like advice on how to evaluate the system.
cards.more: In particular, I am not sure about the study design. Any suggestions are welcome.

cards.q: What was the hardest part of your research?
cards.ja: 研究で一番大変だったことは何ですか。
cards.points: 最も大変だった点
cards.en: The hardest part was collecting data from participants.
cards.more: It took more than three months. Some people stopped in the middle.

cards.q: What have you done so far?
cards.ja: これまでに何をしてきましたか。
cards.points: これまでにやったこと（作ったもの・試したこと）
cards.en: So far, I have built a prototype and tested it with ten users.
cards.more: The first results are promising. Next, I will run a larger study.

cards.q: How does this study fit into your thesis?
cards.ja: この研究は博士論文の中でどんな位置づけですか。
cards.points: 博士論文の中での位置づけ（何番目の研究か）
cards.frame: This study is the ... part of my thesis.
cards.en: This study is the first part of my thesis.
cards.more: It gives the basis for the next two studies. Together, they answer my main research question.

cards.q: What will be the main contribution of your thesis?
cards.ja: 博士論文の主な貢献は何になりますか。
cards.points: 博士論文の主な貢献
cards.en: The main contribution will be a practical method for learning with few labels.
cards.more: I will also show evidence from real users. I think both are important for this field.

cards.q: What would you do differently if you started again?
cards.ja: もう一度始めるなら、何を変えますか。
cards.points: やり直すなら変えること
cards.frame: If I started again, I would ...
cards.en: If I started again, I would run a small pilot study first.
cards.more: I found many problems after the main experiment started. A pilot would have saved a lot of time.
